question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund earns a gross return of 18% on INR 500 cr gross assets. Fund NAV (equity) is INR 250 cr (i.e., 2x leverage). Borrowing cost on the INR 250 cr of borrowed capital = 8% p.a. What is the LEVERED net return on NAV?

explanation.text: The Logic: Gross P&L = 18% * 500 = INR 90 cr. Borrowing cost = 8% * 250 = INR 20 cr. Net P&L = 90 - 20 = INR 70 cr. Levered net return on NAV = 70 / 250 = 28%. Leverage boosted 18% gross to 28% net on equity. The Trap: A subtracts wrong. B ignores leverage. D omits borrow cost. Cross-Exam Context: VIII, XIX-C same. Treasury/FI exams cover identical levered return math. Manager's Pro-Tip: The 28% net-on-equity looks great but the vol also scales ~2x — so Sharpe is similar to the unlevered 18% case. Investors often forget this; present the levered Sharpe (~gross Sharpe, not magnified) to prevent them anchoring on ROE only.
